name: Atmospheric horror / unsettling soundscape from one held MIDI note and one simple synth: a chord MIDI effect stacks two clashing major triads (shifts +4 +7 +13 +17 +20), the two oscillators are spread far apart (+3 and -2 octaves), a low-pass around 170 Hz with resonance about 6, a smooth-random 'wander' LFO on oscillator shape, stereo voice mode, a 100%-wet ping-pong delay with fade on a parallel chain whose rate/time/filter/width are moved by a separate smooth-random LFO with a narrow min/max range, then a large reverb
goal: Build an evolving, clashing, dark soundscape for horror or tense game moments from a single trigger note. Dissonance comes from the polychord, depth from the extreme pitch spread, and motion from smooth-random LFOs whose ranges are clamped so the movement stays understated.

source.title: How to Make HORROR Soundscapes in Ableton Live

prerequisites: A DAW with a chord MIDI effect (or play the six notes), a simple two-oscillator subtractive synth with a smooth-random LFO and mod matrix
Delay with ping-pong and fade/crossfade time mode, a rack or parallel bus, a standalone LFO modulator, a large reverb

inputs.name: trigger_note
inputs.description: Single held note, e.g. C3, one bar or longer

inputs.name: darkness
inputs.description: Filter cutoff target (about 170 Hz in the video, higher reveals the 'electric' buzz)

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Stock device names in the video (a simple subtractive synth, chord MIDI effect, rack/chain, LFO modulator, factory reverb preset) are mapped to generic modules; the downloadable preset is not copied.

The speaker calls it the Elektra chord (C major plus A major). The shifts as spoken (+4 +7 +13 +17 +20 above the root) actually stack C major and C#/Db major. Use the shifts as given, or C plus A major if you want the historical spelling. Both clash strongly.

Steady pitch (Matt's taste): the video also puts the LFO on oscillator 2 detune (about 8%) and on the delay time, which makes pitch moan and wobble. For Matt, leave detune and delay-time modulation off or tiny, and keep the motion on shape, filter, delay filter, feedback and width.
Place reverb first while designing, because it changes the synth decisions.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Trigger one note (C3) with a one-bar or longer MIDI clip into a chord effect that adds the shifts +4, +7, +13, +17, +20.
steps.expect: Six-note clashing polychord from one note

steps.action: Put a large reverb after the synth before you start sound design.
steps.expect: The sound is already wider and less dry, which guides the next steps

steps.action: Pitch spread: oscillator 1 up about +3 octaves and oscillator 2 down about -2 octaves. Use a saturated/sharp shape on the upper oscillator with shape raised. Use a sine on the low oscillator, mixed up about +2.5 dB.
steps.expect: Deep low body under a buzzing, electric top

steps.action: Low-pass down to about 170 Hz with resonance about 6, and clear any default filter modulation.
Set the synth LFO to a smooth-random ('wander') shape and route it fully to the upper oscillator's shape. Switch the voice mode to stereo (voices panned L/R).
steps.expect: Upper partials drift and evolve unpredictably; wider image

steps.action: Parallel delay: wrap a delay in a rack/parallel chain with dry kept, delay 100% wet, feedback about 80%, fade (crossfade) time mode and ping-pong on.
steps.expect: A wide, smeared echo cloud under the dry sound

steps.action: Add a separate smooth-random ('glider') LFO and map it to the delay filter, width, rate and feedback, then turn its depth down so the motion is slow.
steps.expect: Echo cloud slowly changes colour and width

steps.action: Optionally map the LFO to the synth filter cutoff with a narrow min/max window (for example about 33-39%), raising it only to let in more mid frequencies.
steps.expect: Filter breathes in a narrow band without opening to harsh buzz

verification: Rendered bed contains six simultaneous pitches from one MIDI note.
Spectrum mostly sits below a few hundred Hz with resonant emphasis near cutoff; the top buzz stays understated.
Over 60 s the timbre and the echo width change without a repeating cycle.
In the Matt-safe version, pitch tracking shows no detune wobble.
